section: Reddi kingdoms of Addanki, Kondavidu and Rajahmundry - Prolaya Vema Reddi, Kumaragiri Reddi
subsections: Reddi rulers in order and their public works

accepted.s: The Reddi kingdom was established approximately during which period?
accepted.x: The Reddi kingdom flourished approximately from 1325 to 1448 CE. The Kondaveedu line continued from about 1325 to 1424, while the Rajamahendravaram line continued from 1402 to 1448.
accepted.tq: Use the broad chronological range to distinguish the kingdom from the dates of individual ruling lines.
accepted.sec: Reddi rulers in order and their public works

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the principal dynastic features of the Reddis?
o: Panta vamsam, Bull emblem, Mula Guramma as family deity and Sanskrit as royal language
Deseti kula, Garuda emblem, Durga as family deity and Telugu as royal language
Panta vamsam, Lion emblem, Mula Guramma as family deity and Prakrit as royal language
Yadava kula, Bull emblem, Lakshmi as family deity and Kannada as royal language
accepted.x: The Reddis belonged to the Panta vamsam, were also associated with the Deseti kula, used the Bull as their emblem, worshipped Mula Guramma and used Sanskrit as the royal language.
accepted.tq: Match several closely related dynastic identifiers and reject options containing one or more swapped features.
accepted.sec: Reddi rulers in order and their public works

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Reddi dynasty:
1. The Reddis are associated with the Panta vamsam.
2. The Bull was their dynastic emblem.
3. Mula Guramma was their family deity.
4. Sanskrit was the royal language.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The Reddis are identified with the Panta vamsam, the Bull emblem, Mula Guramma and Sanskrit as the royal language.
accepted.tq: Check each statement independently before selecting the comprehensive combination.
accepted.sec: Reddi rulers in order and their public works

accepted.s: Before founding the Reddi kingdom, Prolaya Vema Reddi had served in the court of
accepted.x: Prolaya Vema Reddi had earlier served in the court of Kakatiya ruler Prataparudra.
accepted.tq: Apply the ruler–court association carefully, since dynastic names are a common source of confusion.
accepted.sec: Reddi rulers in order and their public works

accepted.s: Which one of the following was an important measure associated with Prolaya Vema Reddi?
accepted.x: Prolaya Vema Reddi is associated with the establishment of agraharas. The abolition of the gold tax and revival of Motupalli are associated with Anavota Reddi, while the Rajahmundry division was carved out under Kumaragiri.
accepted.tq: Separate the contributions of successive rulers rather than associating every public measure with the founder.
accepted.sec: Reddi rulers in order and their public works

accepted.s: The Manyapuram inscription is particularly associated with which event in Reddi history?
o: The restoration of Veerabhadra Reddi in 1429
The establishment of Addanki as the first capital by Prolaya Vema Reddi
The shifting of the capital from Addanki to Kondavidu by Anavota Reddi
The creation of the Rajahmundry division by Kumaragiri Reddi
accepted.x: The Manyapuram inscription records the shifting of the capital to Kondavidu by Anavota Reddi.
accepted.tq: Link an inscription with the specific administrative event it records, not merely with the dynasty.
accepted.sec: Reddi rulers in order and their public works

accepted.s:
Which of the following measures is correctly associated with Anavota Reddi?
1. Revival of the Motupalli port
2. Abolition of the tax on gold
3. Adoption of the title ‘Dweepa Vijetha’
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Anavota Reddi revived the Motupalli port, abolished the tax on gold and bore the title ‘Dweepa Vijetha’.
accepted.tq: Cluster the administrative, commercial and titulary facts belonging to one ruler before choosing the code.
accepted.sec: Reddi rulers in order and their public works

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Anavema Reddi — Anavemagiri mandapas at Simhachalam
Kumaragiri Reddi — Veerashiro Mantapa at Srisailam
accepted.x: Anavema Reddi built the Anavemagiri mandapas at Simhachalam. The Veerashiro Mantapa is also associated with Anavema, Vasantotsavams with Kumaragiri and Motupalli works with Anavota.
accepted.tq: Use the ruler–public work association and watch for swapped builders.
accepted.sec: Reddi rulers in order and their public works

accepted.s: Anavema Reddi is regarded as the greatest Reddi ruler primarily because of his
o: introduction of the gold tax and naval expansion
patronage of Vasantotsavams and authorship of musical works
establishment of the Rajahmundry line and construction of Motupalli
wide conquests and extensive charitable activities
accepted.x: Anavema Reddi is described as the greatest Reddi ruler because of his widest conquests and large charities, including Brahmanda, Kanakadhara and Gosahasra gifts.
accepted.tq: Identify the distinguishing combination of achievements rather than a single isolated work.
accepted.sec: Reddi rulers in order and their public works

accepted.s: The Veera Siromandapam at Srisailam was built by
accepted.x: Anavema Reddi built the Veera Siromandapam, also referred to as the Veerashiro Mantapa, at Srisailam.
accepted.tq: Apply the builder–monument association without confusing it with Prolaya Vema’s steps at Srisailam.
accepted.sec: Reddi rulers in order and their public works

accepted.s:
Arrange the following Reddi rulers according to their periods of rule in the Kondaveedu line, beginning with the earliest:
A. Anavema Reddi
B. Prolaya Vema Reddi
C. Pedakomati Vema Reddi
D. Kumaragiri Reddi
accepted.x: The order is Prolaya Vema Reddi, Anavema Reddi, Kumaragiri Reddi and Pedakomati Vema Reddi.
accepted.tq: Anchor the sequence with the founder and then place the later rulers by their reign periods.
accepted.sec: Reddi rulers in order and their public works

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about Kumaragiri Reddi is NOT correct?
o: He was the scholar-king who drove out Kumaragiri.
He set up the Rajahmundry division under his son Anavota.
accepted.x: Statement d is not correct because Kumaragiri was driven out by Pedakomati Vema Reddi, who was known as the scholar-king. Kumaragiri patronised dance, held Vasantotsavams and established the Rajahmundry division under his son Anavota.
accepted.tq: Find the statement that assigns a ruler’s own deed to the wrong ruler.
accepted.sec: Reddi rulers in order and their public works

accepted.s: Kumaragiri Reddi initially set up the Rajahmundry division under which person?
accepted.x: Kumaragiri Reddi first set up the Rajahmundry division under his son Anavota Reddi; Kataya Vema later succeeded in administering the division.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the first administrator of a division from its later rulers.
accepted.sec: Reddi rulers in order and their public works

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relationship between the two principal Reddi ruling lines?
o: The Rajahmahendravaram line ended before the Kondaveedu line began.
The Kondaveedu line lasted approximately from 1325 to 1424, while the Rajahmahendravaram line lasted from 1402 to 1448.
The Kondaveedu line lasted from 1402 to 1448, while the Rajahmahendravaram line lasted from 1325 to 1424.
Both lines began in 1325 and ended together in 1424.
accepted.x: The Kondaveedu line ruled approximately from 1325 to 1424, whereas the Rajahmahendravaram line existed from 1402 to 1448.
accepted.tq: Compare overlapping dynastic timelines instead of treating the kingdom as a single uninterrupted line.
accepted.sec: Reddi rulers in order and their public works

accepted.s: The Rajamahendravaram branch of the Reddis was founded by
o: Pakanati Reddis who moved east under Anavota and Anavema
Yadava chiefs who entered the region under Kumaragiri
Kondaveedu Reddis who moved west under Pedakomati Vema
Kakatiya nobles who migrated under Prolaya Vema
accepted.x: The Rajamahendravaram branch was founded by Pakanati Reddis who moved east under Anavota and Anavema.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct migrating branch and the rulers under whom the migration occurred.
accepted.sec: Reddi rulers in order and their public works

accepted.s: Who carved out the Rajahmundry division from his eastern conquests?
accepted.x: Kumaragiri Reddi carved out the Rajahmundry division from his eastern conquests.
accepted.tq: Separate the creation of a territorial division from the later rule of that division.
accepted.sec: Reddi rulers in order and their public works

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the early rulers of Rajamahendravaram:
1. Anavota Reddi was the first ruler of the division.
2. Anavota Reddi died young.
3. Kataya Vema Reddi succeeded him in 1395.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Anavota Reddi, Kumaragiri’s son, was the first ruler of the division, died young, and was followed by Kataya Vema Reddi in 1395.
accepted.tq: Track succession through a short regional line and verify each chronological detail.
accepted.sec: Reddi rulers in order and their public works

accepted.s: Kataya Vema Reddi was killed in the Battle of Kakaraparthi by
accepted.x: Kataya Vema Reddi was killed at Kakaraparthi in 1414 by Gajaraju Tippa, who was an ally of Pedakomati Vema Reddi.
accepted.tq: Use the battle–opponent association and avoid confusing the principal ruler with his ally.
accepted.sec: Reddi rulers in order and their public works

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Kataya Vema Reddi:
1. He ruled Rajamahendravaram from 1395 to 1414.
2. He became independent after 1402.
3. He was killed at Kakaraparthi in 1414.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Kataya Vema ruled from 1395 to 1414, became independent after 1402 and was killed at Kakaraparthi in 1414.
accepted.tq: Test a ruler through the combined use of reign, political status and terminal event.
accepted.sec: Reddi rulers in order and their public works

accepted.s: Who functioned as regent of the Rajamahendravaram state after the death of Kataya Vema Reddi?
accepted.x: Allada Reddi served as regent after Kataya Vema’s death and administered the state for Veerabhadra Reddi.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a regent from the nominal monarch and the de facto ruler.
accepted.sec: Reddi rulers in order and their public works

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Veerabhadra Reddi’s position in Rajamahendravaram?
o: He was the prime minister and de facto ruler from 1423 to 1448.
He was the regent who ruled for Kataya Vema after 1414.
He was the first ruler and died young before 1395.
He was the nominal king and was restored in 1423 and 1429.
accepted.x: Veerabhadra Reddi was the nominal king of Rajamahendravaram and was restored in 1423 and again in 1429.
accepted.tq: Separate nominal authority, regency and de facto power in a divided succession.
accepted.sec: Reddi rulers in order and their public works

accepted.s: Vema, also called Veda, Reddi was the
o: first ruler of the Rajahmundry division
ally who killed Kataya Vema at Kakaraparthi
prime minister and de facto ruler of Rajamahendravaram
accepted.x: Vema or Veda Reddi, the brother of Veerabhadra Reddi, served as prime minister and became the de facto ruler of Rajamahendravaram from 1423 to 1448.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the de facto administrator from the nominal ruler of the same branch.
accepted.sec: Reddi rulers in order and their public works

accepted.s: Allada Reddi received assistance in eastern administration from which group?
o: His sons Vema Reddi, Veerabhadra Reddi and Doddareddi
His brothers Anavota Reddi, Kataya Vema and Kumaragiri
Gajaraju Tippa, Pedakomati Vema and Veda Reddi
Prolaya Vema, Anavema and Racha Vema
accepted.x: Allada Reddi’s helpers in the east were his sons Vema Reddi, Veerabhadra Reddi and Doddareddi.
accepted.tq: Use the family relationship to identify the correct administrative group.
accepted.sec: Reddi rulers in order and their public works
